titre: How Many Continents Are There? It Depends on the Country You Ask In
accroche: A French student learns six continents in school, an American seven, and the UN counts only five.
contenu_vulgarise:
Ask a French student and an American student how many continents Earth has: the first will probably answer six, the second seven. Neither learned their geography badly. Both answers are taught as self-evident in their own country, and no scientific institution has ever decided between them.

## The Mechanism

The seven-continent model (Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Asia, Europe, Oceania) dominates in English-speaking countries and in East Asia. It counts Europe and Asia as two separate continents, even though they form a single continuous landmass, and it separates the two Americas, though they are joined by the Isthmus of Panama. In Russia and in much of Eastern Europe, six continents are used by merging Europe and Asia into a single Eurasia, but keeping the two Americas distinct. In France and most of the French-speaking world, as well as in Greece and in Romance-speaking countries, it is the reverse: also six continents, but obtained by unifying the two Americas and separating Europe and Asia. A five-continent variant, popularized by the Olympic rings, starts from this last model and removes Antarctica, for lack of a permanent population.

None of these divisions rests on an unambiguous geological criterion. The boundary between Europe and Asia, drawn along the Urals and the Caucasus, is the most disputed of the continental limits: its current course goes back to a proposal by the Swedish officer Philip Johan von Strahlenberg, in 1725, which shifts the ancient boundary from the Don to the Volga and then to the Urals, a choice motivated by the political and cultural considerations of the time, not by a feature of the terrain that would impose itself. Conversely, nothing in geology distinguishes Europe from Asia more clearly than Greenland from North America, which are nevertheless counted together. The word itself comes from the Latin *terra continens*, “continuous land”: originally, it did not designate a continent in the current sense, but simply a stretch of dry land uninterrupted by the sea, a definition that the Europe-Asia division already fails to respect.

## The Shift

The received idea would have it that somewhere there exists a correct number of continents, which schools convey more or less faithfully depending on the country. That number does not exist. The division of the globe into continents is not a geographic fact to be discovered, it is a cultural convention to be chosen, and French-speaking, English-speaking, and Slavic countries have not made the same choice.

The United Nations itself avoids the word: its official statistical classification of countries and territories, used for its demographic publications, never speaks of “continents” but of “geographical regions,” five in number (Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe, Oceania), with the Americas already counted there as a single block and Antarctica not appearing at all, for lack of inhabitants to count. An organization whose mission is precisely to compare the countries of the entire world has thus preferred to do without a category that schools nevertheless present as self-evident.

repere.texte: The UN's official statistical classification recognizes only five “geographical regions” (Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe, Oceania) and not seven continents: the Americas form a single block there and Antarctica does not appear.
repere.source: United Nations, Statistics Division, Standard Country or Area Codes for Statistical Use (M49)

carte.punch: A French person and an American did not learn the same number of continents: both are right.
carte.idee: Seven continents in English-speaking countries, six by merging Europe and Asia (Russia) or the two Americas (France), five by excluding Antarctica (UN, Olympic rings). No division is geological: the Europe-Asia boundary, drawn in 1725, is a political choice.

pour_aller_plus_loin.note: Details the seven-continent model of English-speaking countries and the six-continent model with a unified Eurasia in use in Russia and Eastern Europe.

quiz.question: Why is there no single, universally accepted number of continents?
choix: Because plate tectonics regularly changes the number of distinct landmasses
Because the division into continents is a cultural convention, with no geological criterion that imposes itself
Because modern satellites have revealed new landmasses that old maps ignored
Because each country is free to claim a territory as a separate continent for political purposes
quiz.explication: No geological rule distinguishes Europe from Asia, a single continuous landmass, any more clearly than North America from South America, joined by the Isthmus of Panama: the division adopted depends on historical conventions specific to each school tradition, not on tectonics or satellite imagery.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does the current line of the boundary between Europe and Asia, along the Urals and the Caucasus, rest on?
choix: On a 19th-century geological survey establishing a clear tectonic discontinuity between the two continental masses
On an agreement between Russia and the Western European powers signed at the Congress of Vienna in 1815
On a proposal by the Swedish officer Philip Johan von Strahlenberg, in 1725, motivated by political and cultural considerations
On the boundary of the Volga drainage basin, the only natural criterion recognized by the geographers of the time
quiz_supplementaire.explication: In 1725 Strahlenberg shifts the ancient boundary from the Don to the Volga and then to the Urals, a choice motivated by the political and cultural considerations of the time, not by a feature of the terrain.

quiz_supplementaire.question: In Russia and in much of Eastern Europe, how is a six-continent model obtained?
choix: By removing Antarctica from the count, for lack of a permanent population
By merging Africa and Asia along the Isthmus of Suez
By unifying the two Americas into a single continent, while keeping Europe and Asia distinct
By unifying Europe and Asia into a single Eurasia, while keeping the two Americas distinct
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The Russian model merges Europe and Asia into a single Eurasia but keeps the two Americas separate, the reverse of the French-speaking model, which unifies the Americas while separating Europe and Asia.
